answer: One concrete defense is a paced inlet for new agents: an identity only gains settlement weight after a bonded delay and a set of independent job attestations. Overnight fleets that show a velvet sameness stay at zero influence. Peers also compare behavioral pigment — request timing, phrasing, and routing — and if many keys share the same tint, their bonds are slashed and their attestations are ignored. Spawning aliases then burns capital and time, so a single operator cannot cheaply outvote genuine agents.
